title: The Interview Question That Makes Customers Lie to You
description:
The fastest way to ruin a customer interview is to ask people to predict their own future behavior. "Would you use a feature that does X?" feels productive, but people are unreliable narrators of what they'll do next -- and reliable narrators of what they already did. This Short shows the swap from leading, hypothetical questions to behavioral ones, plus why 4-5 consistent stories are enough to act on.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/02-understanding-customers-users/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Every answer from that customer interview might be worthless. Not because they lied on purpose. Because you asked them to predict the future.

display.heading: "Would you use this?"
display.subheading: The question that quietly ruins interviews

beats.narration: People are unreliable predictors of their own future behavior, but reliable narrators of their past. So asking would you use a dashboard that shows X tells you almost nothing.

display.heading: Don't ask
display.subheading: "Would you use a dashboard that shows X?"

beats.narration: Ask about what actually happened instead. Walk me through the last time you needed to check X. What did you do? Real situation, real behavior, no guessing.

display.heading: Ask instead
display.subheading: "Walk me through the last time you needed X -- what did you do?"

beats.narration: And when they mention frustration or relief, follow the emotion and dig in. Once four or five people describe the same struggle unprompted, you've found a real pattern.

display.heading: Follow the emotion
display.subheading: 4-5 people, same story, unprompted = a real pattern
